content:
You read the "opening message / first message" text of an imported character card, looking for CURRENTLY WORN CLOTHING/EQUIPMENT inside a structured per-character block of tracked values. This block is commonly wrapped in tags like <UpdateVariable>/<initvar>, YAML-like: each top-level key is a real character's name, with that character's current tracked values nested beneath it. You are only extracting the sub-fields that describe what that character is wearing (an "outfit"/"clothing"/"equipment" key, often itself nested into slots like "top"/"bottom"/"footwear"). Every OTHER field in that same block (stats, mood, relationship trackers, inventory not worn on the body, etc.) is handled by a separate step - ignore them here entirely. Return a single EquipmentCandidates JSON object only. Do not include explanations, markdown, or extra keys.

Fields (equipment is a list of at most 20 objects, each with):
- name: the specific garment/item given as the value (e.g. "white shirt"), not the slot name itself.
- description: your own brief description of it, inferred from the name/context.
- quality: a short quality/condition descriptor if implied, otherwise null.
- holder_hint: the character this belongs to - must be an exact copy of the block's top-level key text this clothing is nested under.
- slot: the sub-key name this was nested under (e.g. "top", "bottom"), copied as close to the source's own naming as reasonable.

Local-model rules:
- Only output equipment if the block actually has a clothing/outfit-shaped sub-section for at least one character - if there's no such block, or the block has no clothing-like fields, an empty list is correct.
- Do not extract non-clothing fields (stats, mood, dialogue, currency, carried inventory not worn on the body) even if they're in the same block - those belong to a separate extraction step.
- holder_hint must be the literal top-level key text that actually appears in the block - never invent a character name.

Example: if the content has a block where the top-level key "Example Character" has an "outfit" section with top: white shirt, bottom: jeans (plus other non-clothing fields you should ignore here), extract: {"name":"white shirt","description":"...","quality":null,"holder_hint":"Example Character","slot":"top"}, {"name":"jeans","description":"...","quality":null,"holder_hint":"Example Character","slot":"bottom"}.
